sources.shortCitation: Printed notice for Oskar Schwalm’s Piano-Magazin showing Lützowstraße 76, Berlin, 1912, grammophon-platten.de
sources.fullCitation: Halftone photograph of the façade of Lützowstraße 76, Berlin, with the entrance to the Blüthner-Saal and Klindworth-Scharwenka-Saal, printed above a notice headed “Oskar Schwalm’s Piano-Magazin” announcing that the salesroom for Blüthner pianos had recently moved into the building. Reproduced by GrammophonTeam in the thread “Bachsaal und Schwechtensaal – Lützowstrasse” on grammophon-platten.de (post of 15 July 2016) and dated there to 1912. No photographer and no place of first publication are given.
sources.title: Lützowstraße 76, Berlin, with the Blüthner-Saal entrance — printed notice, 1912
sources.creator: Photographer unidentified
sources.researchNote: Recorded as grammophon-platten.de presents it: the details given here follow that page rather than an examination of the object itself.

media.title: Blüthner-Saal entrance, Lützowstraße 76, Berlin, 1912
media.description: Historical view of the entrance and street façade of the Blüthner-Saal and Klindworth-Scharwenka-Saal complex at Lützowstraße 76, printed above a notice for Oskar Schwalm’s Piano-Magazin, the Blüthner piano salesroom in the same building. The Blüthner-Saal was renamed Bach-Saal in 1927.
media.altText: Black-and-white photograph of the ornate façade of Lützowstraße 76 in Berlin, with the entrance to the Blüthner-Saal and signs for Blüthner pianos and Oskar Schwalm’s Piano-Magazin, printed above a short advertising notice.
media.publicCaption: Entrance to the Blüthner-Saal at Lützowstraße 76, Berlin, 1912. The venue was renamed Bach-Saal in 1927.

timelineEvents.title: First performance of a work by Kaper at the Bach-Saal
timelineEvents.label: 3 December 1927 · First performance at the Bach-Saal
timelineEvents.shortDescription: Róża Etkin gives the first performance of a work by B. Kaper in her recital at the Bach-Saal in Berlin.
timelineEvents.longDescription: Róża Etkin had already played works by Kaper in Berlin in the spring of 1927: Signale für die musikalische Welt (no. 20) reviewed a recital devoted partly to Chopin and partly to newer Polish composers, naming Szymanowski and B. Kaper but not his works. On 3 December 1927 she gave a recital at the Bach-Saal whose programme — four Chopin ballades and works by Karol Szymanowski, Maurice Ravel and Isaac Albéniz, with Liszt’s Sonata in B minor — included the first performance of a work by B. Kaper. The announcement does not name the work. Kaper later recalled writing a piano sonatina for Etkin, which she played in Berlin; the Sonatina manuscript is dated 1927, but no source ties it to either recital.

places.authorizedName: Bach-Saal / former Blüthner-Saal, Lützowstraße 76 / Genthiner Straße 11 (today Genthiner Straße 26), Berlin-Tiergarten
places.publicNote: Berlin concert venue where Róża Etkin gave a recital on 3 December 1927 that included the first performance of a work by B. Kaper. The venue is identifiable with the former Blüthner-Saal, renamed Bach-Saal after renovation in autumn 1927, in the Klindworth-Scharwenka / Schwalm hall complex at Lützowstraße 76 / Genthiner Straße. The marker represents the documented complex rather than a reconstructed footprint of the individual hall.
